_meta.description: Curated legal knowledge layer used for scenario routing, applicability reasoning and graph relationships. Every constitutional quote below is checked verbatim against the ingested Constitution text at build time; entries whose quote is not found are stored as 'unverified' and are never used as authoritative evidence. Statutory excerpts are verified only if the official India Code PDF is present in data/statutes and contains the excerpt. Scenario-to-provision mappings are editorial routing hints prepared with AI assistance and are marked 'needs_legal_review'; they decide what to retrieve, never what the law says.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: “the State” includes the Government and Parliament of India and the Government and the Legislature of each of the States and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India
provision_annotations.note: Defines 'the State' for Part III. Most Fundamental Rights restrain 'the State', so whether an actor falls within this definition is usually the first applicability question.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: The State shall not make any law which takes away or abridges the rights conferred by this Part
provision_annotations.note: Laws inconsistent with Part III are void to the extent of the contravention.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: “law” includes any Ordinance, order, bye-law, rule, regulation, notification, custom or usage having in the territory of India the force of law
provision_annotations.note: Defines 'law' for Article 13.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws
provision_annotations.note: Addressed to the State. Relevant to private disputes only through the conduct of State authorities, such as police or officials.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: The State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them
provision_annotations.note: Clause (1) binds the State only.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: No citizen shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them, be subject to any disability, liability, restriction or condition with regard to
provision_annotations.note: Clause (2) is not limited to the State, but it covers only the listed matters: shops, public restaurants, hotels, places of public entertainment, and wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads and places of public resort maintained out of State funds or dedicated to public use. Renting private housing is not among the listed matters.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: be ineligible for, or discriminated against in respect of, any employment or office under the State
provision_annotations.note: Applies to employment or office under the State, not private employment.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: “Untouchability” is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden
provision_annotations.note: Not limited to the State; enforcement of disabilities arising from untouchability is an offence punishable in accordance with law.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: All citizens shall have the right
provision_annotations.note: Article 19 rights are guaranteed to citizens and are read with the restrictions in clauses (2) to (6), which concern laws made by the State. Whether a particular private body can be proceeded against depends on whether it is 'the State' under Article 12 or performs public functions; that requires facts and case law not bundled here.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: to freedom of speech and expression
provision_annotations.note: Subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2).

provision_annotations.supporting_text: No person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself
provision_annotations.note: Protections concerning conviction, double jeopardy and self-incrimination.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law
provision_annotations.note: Article 21 restrains deprivation of life or personal liberty otherwise than according to procedure established by law. Its text does not make every private wrong (such as a theft) a constitutional violation; ordinary criminal and civil law govern private wrongs.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years
provision_annotations.note: Duty of the State, in the manner the State determines by law.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice
provision_annotations.note: Safeguards for a person who is arrested. Subject to the exceptions in Article 22(3).

provision_annotations.supporting_text: shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest
provision_annotations.note: Production before a magistrate within 24 hours, excluding journey time. Subject to Article 22(3).

provision_annotations.supporting_text: Nothing in clauses (1) and (2) shall apply
provision_annotations.note: Clauses (1) and (2) do not apply to enemy aliens or to persons arrested or detained under a preventive detention law.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: Traffic in human beings and begar and other similar forms of forced labour are prohibited and any contravention of this provision shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law
provision_annotations.note: The prohibition is not limited to the State, so it can be engaged by a private employer's conduct.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: Nothing in this article shall prevent the State from imposing compulsory service for public purposes
provision_annotations.note: Exception for compulsory service for public purposes, without discrimination on the listed grounds.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment
provision_annotations.note: Applies to employers generally.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: Subject to public order, morality and health and to the other provisions of this Part, all persons are equally entitled to freedom of conscience
provision_annotations.note: Freedom of religion is itself subject to public order, morality, health and other Part III provisions.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed
provision_annotations.note: Constitutional remedy for Fundamental Rights.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: every High Court shall have power, throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction, to issue to any person or authority, including in appropriate cases, any Government
provision_annotations.note: High Courts may issue writs for enforcing Part III rights and for any other purpose.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law
provision_annotations.note: Constitutional right (not a Fundamental Right since the Forty-fourth Amendment) concerning deprivation of property by authority of law; it is not a protection against private theft.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: The provisions contained in this Part shall not be enforceable by any court
provision_annotations.note: Directive Principles are not enforceable by courts but are fundamental in governance.

provision_annotations.supporting_text: provide free legal aid, by suitable legislation or schemes or in any other way
provision_annotations.note: Directive Principle on free legal aid (not itself enforceable in court under Article 37).

provision_annotations.supporting_text: the rights conferred by Part III (except articles 20 and 21)
provision_annotations.note: During an Emergency the President may suspend enforcement of Part III rights other than Articles 20 and 21.

statutes.title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
statutes.authority: India Code, Legislative Department, Government of India

sections.heading: Theft
sections.text: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.

sections.heading: Unlawful compulsory labour
sections.text: Whoever unlawfully compels any person to labour against the will of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

sections.heading: Wrongful confinement
sections.text: Whoever wrongfully confines any person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.

statutes.title: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
statutes.authority: India Code, Legislative Department, Government of India

sections.heading: Information in cognizable cases
sections.text: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, irrespective of the area where the offence is committed, may be given orally or by electronic communication to an officer in charge of a police station

sections.heading: Copy of information to informant
sections.text: A copy of the information as recorded under sub-section (1) shall be given forthwith, free of cost, to the informant or the victim.

sections.heading: Refusal to record information
sections.text: Any person aggrieved by a refusal on the part of an officer in charge of a police station to record the information referred to in sub-section (1), may send the substance of such information, in writing and by post, to the Superintendent of Police concerned

sections.heading: Magistrate may order investigation
sections.text: Any Magistrate empowered under section 210 may, after considering the application supported by an affidavit made under sub-section (4) of section 173, and after making such inquiry as the Magistrate thinks necessary and the submission made in this regard by the police officer, order such an investigation

sections.heading: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest
sections.text: Every police officer or other person arresting any person without warrant shall forthwith communicate to him full particulars of the offence for which he is arrested or other grounds for such arrest.

sections.heading: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation
sections.text: When any person is arrested and interrogated by the police, he shall be entitled to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation, though not throughout interrogation.

statutes.title: Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976
statutes.authority: India Code, Legislative Department, Government of India

sections.heading: Abolition of bonded labour system
sections.text: On the commencement of this Act, the bonded labour system shall stand abolished and every bonded labourer shall, on such commencement, stand freed and discharged from any obligation to render any bonded labour.

Contravention of the prohibition of forced labour (Article 23)

authorities.name: Officer in charge of a police station

remedies.name: Report the offence to the police and obtain a copy of the recorded information
If the police station refuses to record it, send the substance in writing by post to the Superintendent of Police
Apply to an empowered Magistrate, who may order an investigation
Insist on the statutory arrest safeguards (grounds of arrest, meeting an advocate)
Writ petition to the High Court (for example habeas corpus or mandamus)
Petition to the Supreme Court to enforce a Fundamental Right
Approach the District Magistrate about bonded or forced labour
Use the institution's own grievance or appeal procedure and its governing rules

legal_issues.name: Theft or other property crime by a private person

engages.rationale: Relevant only if a State authority (for example the police) treats the complaint arbitrarily or discriminatorily.

missing_facts: whether the police refused to register or act on the complaint
the place and time of the incident
identifying details of the property (for a phone, the IMEI number)

legal_issues.name: Police refusal to register a complaint

engages.rationale: Equal protection of the laws may be relevant if the refusal is arbitrary or discriminatory; a single refusal does not establish a violation.
High Court writ jurisdiction over public authorities.

missing_facts: whether the information discloses a cognizable offence
whether the refusal was recorded or witnessed

legal_issues.name: Arrest or detention safeguards

engages.rationale: Grounds of arrest and access to a legal practitioner.
Production before a magistrate within 24 hours.
Clauses (1) and (2) do not apply to enemy aliens or preventive detention.
Deprivation of personal liberty must be according to procedure established by law.
Protection against self-incrimination for an accused.

missing_facts: whether the arrest was under a preventive detention law
whether a warrant was shown
whether and when you were produced before a magistrate
whether you are still in custody

legal_issues.name: Discrimination by a private person or business

engages.rationale: Reaches private conduct only for the listed matters (shops, public restaurants, hotels, places of public entertainment, public wells, roads and places of public resort).
Only if the conduct is a practice of untouchability.

missing_facts: whether the landlord or business is a government or public body
the State or city (some local laws may apply)
what was said or written and any evidence of the reason for refusal

legal_issues.name: Discrimination by a government body
missing_facts: which authority acted and what decision was made
whether the decision was in writing

legal_issues.name: Practice of untouchability or caste-based exclusion

engages.rationale: Untouchability is abolished and its enforcement is an offence.

missing_facts: where it happened and who was involved

engages.rationale: Freedom of speech and expression of citizens, generally enforced against the State.
Writs may issue to 'any person or authority'; whether a private institution is amenable depends on facts and case law.
